author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Arabia’s crude supply dropped by 2.3 million barrels per day in August to 6 million barrels per day, its lowest level in more than three decades, the International Energy Agency said Friday. The estimate reflects oil reaching the market and domestic facilities, not simply wellhead production.

The IEA attributed the decline to attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes. Targets included the Jazan refinery, vessels near Yanbu and the Abqaiq processing site, while traffic through Bab el-Mandeb faced additional pressure from groups linked to Yemen’s Houthis.

Saudi Arabia supplied a different figure to OPEC, reporting 7.122 million barrels per day and production of 6.238 million barrels per day in August. Methodology helps explain part of the gap: supply includes exports, withdrawals from storage and crude used in domestic refineries and power plants.

The IEA reduced its forecast for average Saudi crude supply in 2026 by 885,000 barrels per day to 7.6 million. It also estimated that monthly Saudi loadings fell by 1.1 million barrels per day to 3.5 million. The figures add a verified measure of physical-market strain as traders assess damaged infrastructure and risks to multiple Middle East shipping corridors.
dek: The agency estimated August supply at 6 million barrels per day and cut its 2026 forecast as damaged routes and facilities constrained output reaching market.
headline: IEA says Saudi crude supply fell to three-decade low after attacks
